media.altText: Black-and-white photograph of the film director Joseph H. Lewis seated on a film set beside a camera.
media.publicCaption: Joseph H. Lewis, director of The Spy Ring (1938), photographed on the set of The Undercover Man in 1949. The Spy Ring is linked to Kaper only as probable stock-music context, not as a confirmed Kaper credit.
media.publicCreditLine: Photographer unidentified, on the set of The Undercover Man, 1949; via Wikimedia Commons.
media.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared. The Wikimedia Commons file carries a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 2.0 licence attributed to a Flickr account, but a Flickr user cannot license a studio production still made in 1949, so that licence is not relied on here. The underlying photograph is a United States studio still from 1949, inside the 1931–1963 window in which copyright had to be renewed; no renewal has been checked, so its status is unverified rather than known to be free. A reduced-resolution reproduction (320 × 220 px, from 418 × 288 px) is used here for scholarly identification.
